repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
fired := false
if (fired == true) {
    wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == false)
    fired = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
fired = true

diagnosis.summary: The candidate implements a periodic `if` check instead of a rising-edge wait. At t=100ms, the motion sensor was already true, but the candidate only evaluates the `if` condition at the start of the 1000ms wrapper period (t=0). Consequently, it missed the rising edge event that occurred at t=100ms, failing to emit the required `movetobrightness` action. The IR requires blocking on the rising edge before executing the body.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic polling `if` structure with the required rising-edge state machine: persist a `fired` flag, block until the predicate drops to false (rearm), block until the predicate rises to true, execute the body, and mark as fired. This ensures the action triggers exactly when the transition to `true` occurs, matching the IR's `wait(cond, edge rising)` semantics.
